still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US; generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there (maintenance $199).

The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot has not been revived, Congress has not reopened the ~$41B CBO-scored permanent Medicare benefit, and Medicare still pays for no incretin prescribed for weight loss alone.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban in force, and the suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Cycling arithmetic: 42.5% ever-used − 32.1% current = 10.4% of adults who used and are off now. About 50% of current users are on a second or later course (16.05 points), and 3.0 points have cycled and are off again, so (16.05 + 3.0) / 42.5 ≈ 44.8% of ever-users have cycled. The other 7.4 points stopped once and have not restarted. Ever-use rose 7.9 points while current use rose 7.4, so the off-now pool grew only 0.5 points (9.9 → 10.4). Three things hold stopping down: monthly MariTide in clinic tracks (~60% one-year persistence), HRSA programme restarts drawn from the off pool (~0.7M of its 2.0M enrollees are restarters), and oral one-year persistence still near one-third with 36–47% restarting within a year. Age check: 0.20×19.5 + 0.33×32.5 + 0.24×46 + 0.23×28 = 3.9 + 10.7 + 11.0 + 6.4 ≈ 32.1. Income thirds average (39 + 32 + 25.3)/3 ≈ 32.1. Users: 32.1% of ~276M adults ≈ 88.6M. FICTIONAL payer mix: commercial ~15.2M (17%, down from 16.5M, of which ~7.1M are in conditioned tracks, down from 9.4M); Medicare ~16.3M (18%); Medicaid ~6.0M (6.8%, ~1.4M on the AUD label); HRSA Community Metabolic Health Program ~2.0M (2.3%); VA/TRICARE/IHS ~0.8M (now counted separately; earlier steps folded it into commercial and cash); legitimate cash ~41.8M (47%, incl. ~9M on the $149 TrumpRx starting dose indefinitely, ~3.4M on calm/focus plans, ~4.6M on direct-pay MariTide, ~3.9M on cash oral amycretin); imported or counterfeit ~6.5M (7.3%, up from 5.8M as employer retreat outweighed the tariff). Sum: 15.2 + 16.3 + 6.0 + 2.0 + 0.8 + 41.8 + 6.5 = 88.6. On-label AUD users ≈ 4.0M across payers. Adult obesity ~31.0%. About 17% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug, concentrated in the rural South and West outside FQHC reach, and in 65+ adults without qualifying codes. Pediatric: 2.2% of under-18s are on a drug, ~4.0% of 12–17s and ~0.9% of 6–11s. About 62% of 6–11 starts are Medicaid/CHIP. About 6.1M children live with a parent who has regained after stopping. Employer retreat moved ~2.3M people out of tracks: ~0.9M to $149–199 TrumpRx cash, ~0.6M to gray product, ~0.8M stopped.

access.public_coverage: Medicare (~16.3M users) still pays only through diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA, dementia-risk (obesity plus established CVD) and AUD codes, all behind prior authorisation. FICTIONAL arithmetic: 16.3M × ~$232 average net/month × 12 ≈ $45.4B gross Part D incretin spend before rebate true-up (up from ~$38.3B). Net prices stopped falling and the mix shifted toward amycretin. Dementia route: ~2.4M × $240 × 12 ≈ $6.9B. AUD route: ~1.1M × $205 × 12 ≈ $2.7B. Growth slowed after CMS's audit (Oct 2035) found ~19% of sampled AUD claims had nothing behind them but a telehealth AUDIT-C. From Jan 2036, clinicians must attest that DSM-5 criteria are met. Medicaid (~6.0M): AUD oral semaglutide is still a covered outpatient drug in every state. ~6.0M × ~$165 net × 12 ≈ $11.9B. 7 states still cover adult weight-loss use. NEW federal subsidy: the HRSA Community Metabolic Health Program (FY2036 omnibus, $4.3B/yr) supplies the Wegovy pill free at FQHCs to adults at or below 200% FPL who are uninsured or whose Medicaid excludes weight loss, with BMI ≥30 or an AUD diagnosis. HRSA pays TrumpRx prices. ~2.0M enrolled by Dec 2036 at an ~$172 blended starting/maintenance cost: 2.0M × $172 × 12 ≈ $4.1B annualised, at the cap, with waitlists in Mississippi, Alabama and the Rio Grande Valley. New Mexico funds a free AUD pill from its alcohol excise (~45k enrollees). Two state Medicaid programmes still condition coverage.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide still sells for $4–30 a month inside India and in 100+ export markets. Chinese tirzepatide-analogue vials are $20–60 where patents are not enforced. Delivered to US addresses under the Section 232 tariff and Indian export-licence regime, the price is unchanged at ~$90–180. Canadian generics are CAD 45–80 and Brazilian BRL 160–280. India and China supply roughly two-thirds of world incretin volume.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Business Group on Health (Nov 2036): 26% of employers cover weight-management use, down from 33% in 2034. ~70% of those condition coverage on adherence or progress, so unconditional coverage is ~8%. ~94% of employer plans still cover incretins for type 2 diabetes and ~72% for CV risk reduction with established CVD, so coverage has concentrated on codes. ~14% of large employers replaced coverage with a taxable $75–125/month 'metabolic stipend' usable at TrumpRx or direct-to-consumer channels. Prices stalled. Novo and Lilly held 2036 US net prices flat for the first time since 2026, after the Delaware patent ruling (Mar 2035) and Amgen's MariTide capacity limits. TrumpRx: Wegovy pill $149 starting, $199 maintenance. Foundayo $149–229. Injectable Wegovy/Zepbound $249–299. MariTide $249/month direct, unchanged, with q8-week maintenance at $249 per dose. Oral amycretin is still ~$449 cash with a $1,299 list price and no TrumpRx price; ~8.5M users. Retatrutide ~$399. Orals ~52% of users, weekly injectables ~37%, monthly/q8-week MariTide ~11% (~9.6M). Gray market: delivered prices flat. Domestic re-filling from smuggled API persists, and counterfeits are a larger share.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1/amylin unimolecular co-agonist, daily oral (oral amycretin)
GLP-1 agonist/GIP-receptor antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable with every-8-week maintenance and home autoinjector (maridebart cafraglutide: MariTide, new regimen approved Jun 2035)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
Activin type II receptor antibody muscle adjunct (bimagrumab, restricted label)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: moderate-to-severe alcohol use disorder (oral semaglutide / Wegovy pill). The VA/DoD guideline (Jul 2035) lists it first-line alongside naltrexone. A tirzepatide AUD sNDA was filed Dec 2035; its PDUFA date was extended to Jan 2037 after a major amendment adding fracture data
pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics; weekly semaglutide), with growth, Tanner and eating-disorder monitoring

reduction of risk of all-cause dementia in adults with obesity and established CVD (tirzepatide). The 60+ without-CVD extension received a complete response letter in Sep 2035 citing hip fractures in women 70+
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'calm' and 'focus' low-dose plans via telehealth (~3.4M subscribers, ~40% written on the AUD label)
dementia-prevention use by 55–75-year-olds without CVD, cash-paid, continuing despite the CRL
indefinite use of the $149 TrumpRx starting dose (~9M people, ~1.3M of them through the HRSA programme)
above-label semaglutide dosing in 12–14-year-olds in gray channels
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. The monthly/implant driver is realised with an existing product in a new form. In Jun 2035 FDA approved MariTide every-8-week maintenance after 12 months of monthly dosing, plus a single-dose home autoinjector. Amgen's Holly Springs and New Albany fill-finish capacity limited supply into 2036. Implants are still in phase 2 and not on the US market. Tirzepatide dementia 60+ was resubmitted Feb 2035. The Jul 2035 advisory committee voted 7–6 against, and a CRL followed in Sep 2035 requiring fracture-mitigation data. Lilly is running a bimagrumab co-administration trial. The bimagrumab label expansion to all incretin users 65+ was filed Feb 2036 and is under review, with a decision no earlier than Feb 2037. The tirzepatide AUD sNDA was filed Dec 2035 and is under review. Price stall: in Mar 2035 the District of Delaware upheld Novo's semaglutide formulation and SNAC oral-delivery patents against ANDA filers, and appeals push US generic entry past 2036. Branded net prices, which had fallen 3–5% a year, were flat in 2035–36. Global incretin market ~$215B (2035). No oral matches retatrutide's ~24%.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation outside clinic tracks. Nausea in the 8-week MariTide maintenance window is reported as less frequent than at monthly dosing.

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and bowel obstruction (persistent delayed gastric emptying)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The first two MDL bellwethers (2035) split: a defense verdict in one, an $11M plaintiff verdict in the other, now on appeal. GI claims are ~44,000. Persistence after stopping is still disputed.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No new labelling; no global settlement.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid weight loss; unchanged.
Still no causal confirmation; absolute risk low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; pleaded within the EPI tort.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The Medicare hip-fracture HR is ~1.3 after 2+ years and ~1.45 after 3+ cycles, and ~1.6 in women 75+ with 4+ years of use. The mechanism is accepted: rapid fat-plus-lean loss, reduced mechanical loading, lower protein intake, and EPI malabsorption in some users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Apr 2036 class labeling: a new Warnings & Precautions section on bone loss and fractures, with baseline DXA recommended at 65+ and for anyone continuing beyond 2 years. CMS covers the DXA under a new code. Endocrine Society guidance recommends resistance training, ≥1.2 g/kg protein and antiresorptive therapy when indicated.

safety_ledger.effect: Population fracture, falls and frailty burden in older and long-term users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: CDC/CMS (Apr 2036) report that the age-adjusted hip-fracture rate in Medicare women 75+ rose ~4% from 2033 to 2035, reversing a two-decade decline. Estimated attributable excess: ~16,000–22,000 hip fractures a year among older users, implying ~3,000–4,000 deaths within a year at standard post-fracture mortality. Fall-related ED visits are up in Sun City, AZ and The Villages, FL catchments. About 0.42M people are on bimagrumab, which costs ~$1,100 list and is covered by Medicare only with a fracture-risk code.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labeling as above. The tirzepatide dementia 60+ CRL (Sep 2035). The bimagrumab expansion is under review. No REMS, no age cap.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new adult signal through three years of AUD-label use.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~7% clinically meaningful anhedonia at maintenance doses vs ~3.5% in controls, ~10% on retatrutide. In 2035 FDA commissioned a low-dose study using platform cohorts; it is enrolling, with no readout yet. The low-dose rate is still unmeasured, now across ~3.4M calm subscribers and ~9M indefinite starting-dose users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No labelling change; three more untitled letters; no enforcement.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, worse after cycles. A new regain cohort of ~0.8M people stopped after losing employer coverage in 2035–36.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; it is the rationale for conditioned and clinic-administered coverage.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron, vitamin D and thiamine (AUD users who keep drinking). Low protein intake is now linked explicitly to fracture risk. Low ferritin in adolescent girls.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Annual micronutrient panel language; protein counselling added in the Apr 2036 class labeling.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~2× incidence after 5+ years on semaglutide; tirzepatide HR ~1.3. EPI claims are ~68,000. DOJ's civil investigative demand to Novo is unresolved. The Novo reserve was raised to ~$7.4B.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EPI wording on both labels; FDA follow-up inspection closed with no warning letter (2035).

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About fourteen years of semaglutide follow-up now exist. Cycling's effects on bone are now partly characterised; its effects on the pancreas are not. There are still no data on indefinite starting-dose use, which now includes a federal programme. Q8-week dosing adds no long-term data yet.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric bone and growth PMRs continue; HRSA funds a voluntary FQHC outcomes registry.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Non-approved-product adverse-event reports passed ~38,000. A second re-filled-vial infection cluster (2035, Alabama and Georgia, ~90 cases, 1 death). Poison-centre calls are flat.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The tariff and export checks remain; no statute; no state action.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: STEP Young extension at 2 years shows a ~0.5 cm/year height-velocity deficit, with partial catch-up after stopping. The Swedish ARFID HR is ~1.8. Final adult height is unknown.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Monitoring language and medication guide; no REMS; AAP lifestyle-first for prepubertal children.

safety_ledger.effect: Alcohol-related harms on the AUD label (dehydration, alcoholic ketoacidosis, aspiration with vomiting during binge drinking)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~1 per 2,000 person-years during titration, unchanged with ~4.0M on-label users. Falls while intoxicated, combined with drug-related bone loss, are noted in older drinkers.

food_and_beverage.state: About 48% of US households have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~15–17% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~13%. Dollar sales are down ~2% over two years. The 'tariff bounce' in low-income zips partly reversed where HRSA enrolment is dense (Jackson, Birmingham, McAllen). Protein-fortified 'bone' lines (calcium, vitamin D and whey for over-60s) are the fastest-growing grocery subcategory.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes are down ~21% from 2025 and beer ~13%. The VA/DoD first-line listing, Medicaid and New Mexico's free AUD pill reach the heavy-drinking core. Kentucky distillers cut another ~1,100 jobs and Brown-Forman mothballed one Louisville-area rickhouse complex. New Mexico package-store revenue fell ~9% in a year. Non-alcoholic products are ~6% of category dollars.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat. Late-night revenue keeps falling in Midwestern bar districts. Casual dining runs portion tiers. QSR value menus are strong where employer coverage dropped. Senior-living dining contracts add protein minimums after the fracture labeling.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking. Resale and stretch serve cyclers. Hip-protector underwear and fall-safe footwear became a mass-retail aisle at Walmart and CVS in Sun Belt retirement markets. Structured athletic wear keeps growing.

fitness.state: Strength training keeps growing. Medicare Advantage plans fund resistance classes and 'bone clinics' after the Apr 2036 labeling, and FQHCs pair HRSA enrolment with group walking and band classes. Budget gyms run DXA vans. Pediatric family strength programmes stay an upper-income product.

insurance.state: Employers retreat to diabetes and CV codes. Weight-management coverage fell from 33% to 26%, and ~14% of large employers swapped coverage for taxable stipends. Commercial pharmacy trend ~+5%, slower because users moved off the books. Remaining tracks shift to clinic-administered MariTide, where administration verifies adherence and app logs are no longer needed. Part D premiums rose again for 2036. CMS recouped AUD overpayments from three plan sponsors.

pharma.state: Volume grows and prices are flat, which is good for margins. Amgen is capacity-constrained on MariTide. Novo is recovering on oral amycretin despite a ~$7.4B reserve. Lilly absorbed the dementia CRL. Retail pharmacies sell DXA and bimagrumab infusion slots. Indian exporters keep redirecting volume to non-US markets.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: The body still reads as how you are paid. A monthly clinic bruise or an 8-week appointment card means you are still in a track. A $149 slow-thin means cash or the federal clinic pill. A T-score is a new status number among women over sixty. A cane at sixty-eight, in Sun City or The Villages, is now read as 'she was on it too long'. A child's growth chart is still a status document in Bethesda and a clinic form in South Memphis.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Muscle remains the class uniform. Upper-income older users now display bone: DXA results, weighted vests, bimagrumab infusions. The free HRSA pill made slow thinness visible in Jackson and the Rio Grande Valley, where it is called 'the clinic pill' or, by critics, 'federal thin'. The middle third is the squeezed tier: dropped by employers and paying $199–449 cash or going without.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are shorter. Senior centres and church suppers add protein targets. Bread Alone claims ~1,400 congregations, and its 'full table' suppers now draw older women alongside young families. Pill nights persist in Dayton and Toledo bars.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: App tags now include 'monthly' as well as 'calm plan' and 'on AUD treatment'. Among older daters 'strong bones' is a profile line. Couples where one partner lost employer coverage report a new mismatch: one partner stays on the drug, the other regains.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: In the upper tier, appetite and craving are still noise a subscription manages. In the South, appetite politics flipped: the 'hunger tax' grievance met a federal free pill, and the fight now is whether that pill is relief or 'pharma welfare'. The backlash added a new constituency: older women with fractures, organised as 'Stand Tall', joined the second Let Them Grow rally (~85,000, Jun 2036). Fat-acceptance revivalists again marched separately in Oakland and Philadelphia.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~7% clinically meaningful anhedonia at maintenance doses vs ~3.5% in controls; ~10% on retatrutide. Calm/focus plans grew to ~3.4M subscribers, paying $149–199 for low-dose Wegovy pill or Foundayo plus $39–59 fees. ~40% are written on the AUD label. After CMS's attestation rule, platforms route Medicare-age applicants to cash and market 'craving-free' to commercially insured drinkers. FDA's low-dose study is enrolling and has no readout. ~9M indefinite starting-dose users are effectively a second, unbranded low-dose population, and ~1.3M of them are federally supplied.
interior_life.framing: Platforms sell 'quiet the noise' and 'quiet the bottle'. Since employer retreat, some sell to employers as a stipend-eligible 'focus benefit'. Manufacturers say 'food noise' and 'reduced heavy drinking days'. HR says steadiness. Clinicians say dose-related blunting. Stand Tall and Unmuted say 'they quieted us and thinned our bones'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: About 7.1M employees remain in conditioned tracks, and most of them are now on clinic MariTide, so adherence is proven by appearance at the clinic rather than by an app. A missed appointment moves the premium tier. Stipend employers market calm plans in open enrolment as a 'focus benefit'. Trucking and warehousing EAPs still offer the AUD pill. FMCSA has issued no calm-plan guidance. The two EEOC charges remain unresolved.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off' memoir and 'dry' stand-up persist. A new genre of older-women fracture memoir ('The Year I Broke') reached bestseller lists. Live-music nights in Louisville and Columbus keep closing. Sportsbook handle per account falls further. Ambient streaming tiers bundle with calm subscriptions.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: The pill window still structures mornings. For monthly users the clinic day replaced the shot date, and couples schedule around it. Therapists still see sober/drinking partner splits, and now caregiver strain where a spouse's fracture follows years of use.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The subsidy made incretins a 2036 campaign issue. Three Senate primary challengers in Tennessee, Kentucky and Ohio ran against the HRSA programme as 'pharma welfare'; one won his primary. Delta Democrats defended it as repayment of the 'hunger tax'. The programme survived in the FY2037 continuing resolution at flat funding. 'Sedated electorate' claims still lack turnout evidence; 2036 turnout data are not yet analysed.

state.regulatory_posture: Federal, routine and permissive on approvals, tighter on labels. FDA approved MariTide's q8-week regimen, added class bone and fracture warnings, and issued the tirzepatide dementia CRL. CMS tightened AUD attestation. No state banned or restricted anything. Illinois's ban is still the only one. Imports are still punished.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: The direct subsidy is new. The HRSA Community Metabolic Health Program ($4.3B/yr, FY2036 omnibus, continued under the FY2037 CR) gives a free Wegovy pill at FQHCs to low-income adults with BMI ≥30 or AUD, ~2.0M enrolled. Continued supply requires a clinic weigh-in every six months and, from 2036, a baseline DXA at 65+. New Mexico funds a free AUD pill from its alcohol excise. OPM's FEHB conditions and the 2027 tri-agency guidance stand.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: The data shifted from app logs to clinic records. MariTide tracks verify adherence by administration. HRSA enrolment feeds a federal FQHC registry: weight, A1c, AUDIT-C and DXA, opt-out for research. CMS's AUD attestation creates a DSM-5 documentation trail. Platforms still sell de-identified focus cohorts to brokers.
state.workforce_or_military: The VA/DoD guideline (Jul 2035) lists oral semaglutide first-line for AUD. TRICARE and the VA cover it. The Army recruit oral pilot is unchanged. FMCSA covers on-label AUD use only.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The Section 232 tariff and the Indian export checks remain. A WTO panel ruled for China in Jul 2036; the US appealed into the defunct Appellate Body, so nothing changes. Novo and Lilly expanded US plants. Amgen's fill-finish lines in North Carolina and Ohio are the binding constraint on monthly supply. Smuggled API keeps domestic re-filling alive.

events.event: Federal court in Delaware upholds Novo's semaglutide formulation and oral-delivery patents against generic filers; Novo and Lilly hold 2036 US net prices flat, ending nine years of decline
FDA approves every-eight-week MariTide maintenance and a home autoinjector; employers' remaining weight tracks move to clinic-administered dosing as Amgen warns of fill-finish shortages into 2036

Business Group on Health: employer weight-loss coverage falls from 33% to 27% for 2036, with large firms limiting incretins to diabetes and heart codes and one in seven offering a cash stipend instead; it reaches 26% a year later

FY2036 omnibus funds a $4.3 billion HRSA programme giving free Wegovy pills at community health centres to low-income adults with obesity or alcohol use disorder, months after the VA/DoD guideline lists the pill first-line for AUD; enrolment hits 2 million and waitlists by late 2036

CDC and CMS report the hip-fracture rate in Medicare women over 75 rising for the first time in two decades; FDA adds class bone-loss and fracture warnings with baseline DXA scans for users 65 and older, following its 2035 rejection of tirzepatide's dementia extension over fractures

Second 'Let Them Grow' rally draws about 85,000 to the Mall, now joined by 'Stand Tall', a bloc of older women with fractures; primary challengers in Tennessee, Kentucky and Ohio campaign against the HRSA programme as 'pharma welfare'

open_tensions: The fracture wave lands on exactly the users Lilly wants for dementia prevention. Bimagrumab costs ~$1,100 a month and Medicare covers it only with a fracture-risk code, while ~2.4M Medicare users on the dementia route and many cash-paying 60-somethings keep going. The first full-year count of attributable hip fractures arrives in 2037.

The federal government now supplies the $149 starting dose indefinitely to ~1.3M people. Nobody has studied that regimen. Funding is one continuing resolution away from a cut, the programme has waitlists, and a cut would produce a regain cohort larger than the tariff's.

With prices frozen and employers retreating, ~42M people pay cash. The middle third is squeezed between $199 and $449 a month. Remaining tracks verify adherence by clinic attendance, so stopping a monthly shot means stopping coverage.

Calm platforms sell blunting with an AUD diagnosis attached. CMS has forced attestation in Medicare, but commercial and cash routes are untouched. Lilly's tirzepatide AUD decision lands in Jan 2037, and the low-dose anhedonia study has not read out.

prose.headline: One in Three, Prices Frozen, a Free Pill for the Poor, and a Spike in Grandmothers' Broken Hips: America's Incretin Ledger, 2036
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2036 about one American adult in three takes an incretin, nearly eighty-nine million people. More than four in ten have tried one. The growth did not come from cheaper drugs, because the drugs stopped getting cheaper. In March 2035 a federal judge in Delaware upheld Novo's formulation patents. Novo and Lilly then held their American net prices flat for 2036, the first year without a cut since the middle of the last decade. The Wegovy pill's starting dose is still $149 through TrumpRx. Oral amycretin, the pill that matches tirzepatide, is still about $449 in cash. Amgen's MariTide is still $249 a dose, and Amgen cannot fill vials fast enough.

The growth came from two directions. Inside the clinics that remain, adherence stopped being a choice. In June 2035 the FDA approved MariTide every eight weeks after a year of monthly dosing, and most employer weight programmes now require it. A nurse gives the shot, the appointment is the proof, and a missed appointment moves your premium tier. Fewer employers run these programmes. Coverage for weight fell from a third of employers to about a quarter. Large firms kept paying for diabetes and heart patients and gave everyone else a taxable stipend and a link to TrumpRx. About forty-two million Americans now pay for the drug themselves, and the middle third of earners feels it most.

At the bottom, Congress did something it had refused to do for Medicare. The December 2035 spending bill created a $4.3 billion programme that hands out the Wegovy pill free at community health centres to low-income adults with obesity or a drinking disorder. Two million people are enrolled. In Jackson and McAllen the waitlists run to spring. Most enrollees take the starting dose and nothing higher. Washington now supplies, at scale, a regimen nobody has studied. Some people in the Delta call it repayment for the tariff that took their vials in 2033. Others call it federal thin.

The alcohol label kept spreading without any new approval. The VA and Defense Department made the pill a first-line treatment for alcohol use disorder, and New Mexico, which has the country's worst drinking deaths, pays for it out of its liquor tax. About four million Americans now take an incretin for drinking. Spirits volumes are down a fifth from 2025. The calm platforms sell 'quiet the bottle' to three and a half million subscribers. After Medicare's auditors found one claim in five had nothing behind it but a screening quiz, they stopped selling to Medicare and sell to the commercially insured instead.

The new story is bones. In April the CDC and CMS reported that hip fractures among Medicare women over seventy-five had risen for the first time in twenty years. The FDA added a class warning and a recommended bone scan at sixty-five. Months earlier it had turned down Lilly's request to market tirzepatide for dementia prevention in healthy sixty-year-olds, citing those same fractures. Analysts estimate the drugs now account for somewhere between sixteen and twenty-two thousand extra broken hips a year. Walmart in Sun City sells hip-protector underwear by the register. Medicare Advantage plans pay for resistance classes. A muscle drug costs eleven hundred dollars a month, and few people get it.

The backlash grew older. In June the second Let Them Grow rally brought eighty-five thousand people to the Mall, and the parents marched beside grandmothers on walkers who call themselves Stand Tall. Three Senate challengers ran against the free pill as pharma welfare, and one won his primary. The programme survived on a stopgap at flat funding. No state banned anything. From a distance the country is thinner, more sober and calmer. Up close, it pays for the drug or gets it free, and in the South it is starting to break its hips.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Tameka Ruffin wakes at 5:40 in Jackson, swallows the pill with a capful of water, and waits thirty minutes for her coffee. The bottle says HRSA under the pharmacy label. It's the same 1.5 milligrams she has taken since February, because the next dose is backordered at the health centre on the boulevard, and nobody there has pushed her to go higher.

By seven she is at Miss Odessa's. Miss Odessa is seventy-nine, has a pin in her left hip since March and a Mounjaro pen in the butter tray that Medicare pays for. Tameka hands her the walker and counts the sit-to-stands out loud. On the fifth one Miss Odessa says, "I used to be so proud of how small I got." Tameka scrambles two eggs and a scoop of the whey powder from the yellow tub. Miss Odessa eats half of it.

At noon she sits in her car and eats a sleeve of crackers, slowly. Two years ago she would have finished the box. In 2033 the vials from the Facebook seller stopped coming, and by Christmas she was back in her old scrubs.

Her daughter texts a picture from school: a flyer for a Full Table supper at Greater Mount Calvary. Bring a dish. No pills at the table.

Tameka goes. She brings green beans. The pastor talks about God making us hungry for a reason. She eats a little of everything and feels nothing pull at her. Driving home, the radio says the clinic programme got funded through March.

She sets the pill and the glass of water on the nightstand for the morning.
